name: NullPoint Technologies SynapseJam SJ-3 'Migraine'
description:
A directed BCI disruption device that fires a focused electromagnetic pulse calibrated to the operating frequencies of common neural interface models. Unlike the omnidirectional NG-1, the SJ-3 is a point-and-shoot device that delivers its disruption field in a narrow cone, affecting only the targeted individual within a five-meter range. The SJ-3's pulse causes a brief but intense disruption of BCI signal processing, manifesting as a 'neural stutter' — a two-to-four-second window during which augmented cognitive functions (enhanced reflexes, threat assessment, sensory processing) experience cascading errors.

The SJ-3 represents NullPoint's second-generation BCI defense technology, incorporating frequency profiles for the forty most common neural interface models in GLMZ. The device automatically scans for BCI signal emissions and adjusts its disruption pulse to match the detected interface's operating frequency, significantly increasing effectiveness compared to the broadband interference of the NG-1. This targeting capability also means the SJ-3 is less likely to affect bystanders' augmentations — though it will still disrupt any BCI system within its cone.

Priced at Φ680, the SJ-3 is a significant investment but has found a market among individuals who have been specifically victimized by augmented criminals and are willing to invest in targeted countermeasures. NullPoint sells the device through security consultants rather than retail channels, partly for liability management and partly to ensure purchasers receive training in appropriate use.
specifications:
disruption range: 5 meters directional cone (15-degree width)
effect: 2-4 second neural stutter (cascading BCI processing errors)
frequency profiles: 40 common neural interface models
auto-detection: scans for BCI signal emissions
pulses per charge: 10
recharge: 2 hours
weight: 145 g
dimensions: 12 cm x 4 cm cylinder
cost: Φ680
tactical_use: Point the device at the augmented attacker and press the activation button. The SJ-3 will auto-detect their BCI frequency and deliver a tuned disruption pulse. The resulting neural stutter causes a two-to-four-second window of impaired cognitive function — use this window to deploy other deterrents or flee. The directed cone means you can target an individual without affecting nearby civilians in most situations. Ineffective against individuals with hardwired-only augmentations or military-grade shielded interfaces.
cultural_context: The SJ-3 has elevated the BCI defense conversation from broad disruption to targeted countermeasures, and this precision has made it simultaneously more socially acceptable and more controversial. Proponents argue that targeting a specific attacker's augmentations is more ethical than disrupting everyone nearby. Opponents argue that the device's frequency-profiling capability is one step from a neural weapon — a tool designed to attack someone's brain. The legal and ethical framework for BCI countermeasures is years behind the technology.
story_hooks: A modified SJ-3 has been recovered that extends the neural stutter duration to minutes rather than seconds — the victim experienced a prolonged cognitive shutdown that caused permanent memory loss around the event.

NullPoint's frequency profile database has been leaked, and black-market developers are using it to create offensive neural attack tools that target specific BCI models with destructive rather than disruptive pulses.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, pistol-like cylinder with a forward-facing emitter array. The design emphasizes precision and directed targeting — nothing like a traditional firearm. It reads as medical-tech crossed with targeting equipment, with a pronounced muzzle cap that houses the focusing array. The overall impression is clinical efficiency: compact, purposeful, slightly intimidating.
physical_description.dimensions: 12 cm length, 4 cm diameter cylinder. Emitter aperture approximately 2.5 cm diameter. Ergonomic grip section 3 cm deep.
physical_description.weight_description: Balanced and light in hand — 145g feels almost insubstantial, making it easy to aim and maintain on target. The weight distribution favors the grip, creating minimal muzzle-heavy sensation.
physical_description.primary_material: Medical-grade polymer composite body with embedded conductive trace patterns visible beneath translucent sections. Forward emitter housing is brushed aluminum alloy with precision-machined focusing rings.
physical_description.finish: Matte charcoal polymer with satin-finish aluminum accents. The emitter cap shows faint oxidation patterns suggesting precision machining marks. Minimal wear-resistant coating.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray body with gunmetal silver emitter ring. Accent lighting: faint blue LED indicators on the grip section (dormant unless active).
physical_description.grip_texture: Soft-touch rubberized polymer with subtle grip stippling. Finger wells are precisely molded. Activation button sits naturally under index finger — textured metal beneath rubber coating for positive feedback.
distinctive_features: Forward-facing electromagnetic focusing rings (3 stacked rings of brushed aluminum)
Translucent polymer sections revealing internal capacitor coils and circuitry
Small blue LED array on grip (status/frequency lock indicator)
Textured metal activation button with slight resistance
Narrow cooling vents along grip section
Micro-laser targeting point on emitter (faint red)
Frequency-lock indicator window showing active profile
Recessed charging port on grip base (gold contacts visible)
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: NullPoint Technologies logo (Φ symbol variant) centered on grip. 'SYNAPSEJAM SJ-3' etched below logo. Serial number stamped on charging port plate. Regulatory compliance stamps in micro-text along barrel. Thin white accent line running along seam between body and grip.
physical_description.condition_typical: Maintained in pristine condition by owners — this is a precision instrument requiring care. Security consultant inventory models show minimal handling wear. Field units may exhibit faint wear on grip stippling and slight scuffing on emitter cap from storage, but typically kept clean and carefully stored.
